slice.name: canonical_payload_receipt_separation
slice.objective: Test whether deterministic immutable candidate identity survives cross-invocation retry when per-invocation timestamps, connector metadata and transient diagnostics differ.
slice.model: Finite deterministic role-local candidate builder. Candidate semantic bytes use canonical JSON over stable semantic fields only; volatile invocation metadata is stored only in a separate immutable receipt. Candidate key K = SHA256(parent_latest_blob || NUL || next_revision || NUL || canonical_semantic_bytes).
slice.verdict: PASS in the tested finite deterministic model. Separating canonical semantic candidate bytes from volatile per-invocation receipt metadata preserves identical candidate bytes and the same deterministic key across retries; the negative control that embeds receipt metadata produces different keys and would create a duplicate candidate path.

comparison.candidate_A: canonical semantic payload + separate immutable receipt
comparison.candidate_B: single payload that embeds volatile receipt metadata
comparison.expected_completion_time: A is one deterministic create/CAS path on retry; B can fork retry identity and add recovery work.
comparison.success_probability: A preserved identity for both tested invocations; B failed the identity invariant by construction.
comparison.conflict_duplication_risk: A low in tested model; B high because volatile metadata changes K.
comparison.integration_cost: A requires two record types but no extra executor; B appears simpler but breaks retry determinism.
comparison.quota_fragility: Neither design requires hosted compute; only lightweight repository transport is assumed, and retry identity does not depend on transport metadata.

tested_scope: Two synthetic invocations with identical stable semantics and deliberately different timestamps, invocation IDs, connector response metadata and transient diagnostics. Tested canonical JSON byte equality and deterministic SHA-256 key equality, plus a negative control embedding receipt metadata. Not tested: ambiguous create outcome where K:B may already have committed, noncanonical semantic serialization, silent-overwrite transports, multi-pointer authority or a live production collision.
conflict_check: Used frozen sanitized DESIRED_STATE control26/blob 481660fb6008a57cea162da38439cf115c8d7ebe, own cross_field config8/blob fd9bcd6e7ffe06fe5b854e08af6158279c80fffc, own LATEST r175/blob 403bb30a4c236110b91f2c32f4dde668fc93f20b and a local deterministic model only. No O/O-derived state, other-worker state/config/receipts, downstream state, legacy research, shared ledger, scheduler or protected-primary semantic input was used or mutated.
candidate_revision: Make canonical candidate semantic bytes a stable, metadata-free object and place timestamps, connector response metadata and transient diagnostics only in a separate immutable receipt. Deterministic retry identity is then a function of frozen parent, next logical revision and canonical semantic bytes only.
frontier: Test ambiguous candidate-create result recovery where K:B may have committed before a transient client failure; require read-at-K exact-byte reconciliation before any second create or pointer CAS.
Then test noncanonical semantic serialization defenses so logically identical semantic objects cannot acquire different candidate keys.
exact_continuation: Next invocation, after manifest/RUN_LIFECYCLE-first bootstrap and exact two-pass authority freeze, read own LATEST r176 only as needed and execute exactly one bounded ambiguous-create-result recovery leaf. Model three post-create client outcomes: confirmed success, confirmed failure-before-commit and ambiguous failure-after-possible-commit. On the ambiguous branch, read deterministic K first; if exact canonical B exists, adopt it and proceed to pointer-last CAS only if the frozen parent is still current; if K is absent, create once; if bytes mismatch, stop with diagnostic and never overwrite. Falsify on duplicate create path, stale-parent adoption or mismatched-byte overwrite. Preserve noncanonical-serialization defense as the following leaf.
